purpose: V1.1.1 had no decision. Next percent-decodes every dynamic route segment before a handler sees it - route-matcher.js does params[key] = match.split('/').map(decode) for a catch-all - and nine handlers decoded again. '%252e%252e' became '..' and '%253f' became '?', which interpolated into an upstream URL carrying the caller's bearer token would put an attacker's query parameter ahead of the caller's own; '%2523' became '#', whose fragment swallows the intended query string entirely.
requiredInvariants: The framework's behaviour is read, not assumed. That Next decodes catch-all segments comes from route-matcher.js in the installed next@15.5.21, quoted in the guard and in the decision.

Reachability is checked before anything is claimed. None of the nine was exploitable: every proxy runs the normalised path past an anchored allowlist whose character classes admit no ?, # or /, so each vector was refused. The finding is that a second control was cleaning up after a wrong first one, and the requirement is about the first.

A guard that misses the shape it was written for is worse than no guard. The first version found four sites a manual survey had missed and reported three others clean, because those put the decode inside a separate normalizePath(segments) and the taint arrived as a function parameter. It now propagates through calls to a fixed point and sees through a || default and parentheses - and each of those steps fails a test when removed.

The guard does not object to decoding something that genuinely arrives encoded. Twenty-one remaining decodes operate on values this application itself encoded - cookies it wrote, the percent-encoded userinfo of a URL, a regex capture from a cookie header - and a rule that flagged those would be switched off.

No behaviour is lost. A legitimate identifier is alphanumeric and the removed decode was a no-op on it; an input carrying a percent sequence was refused by the allowlist before and is refused by it now, since % appears in no character class.
acceptance: V1.1.1: PENDING_APPLICABILITY_REVIEW/NOT_ASSESSED -> APPLICABLE/PASS, exactly one requirement changed. 129 -> 130 PASS, 39 -> 38 NOT_ASSESSED.
Nine second decodes removed across eight route handlers and two page components. The guard reports zero remaining and exits 0.

verify-decode-once.test.mjs passes 13 of 13, including the helper-call shape, the || default, the parenthesised default, and the negative case of decoding a cookie the application encoded. Five mutations each fail it: removing the interprocedural step, not unwrapping ||, not unwrapping parentheses, reducing the fixed point to one pass, and narrowing the decoder list.

The PASS is revocable: restoring one decode in apps/web/app/api/staff/[...path]/route.ts drops V1.1.1 to NOT_ASSESSED and makes the guard exit 1; removing it again restores PASS. The occurrence count was checked before the verdict was read.
The web suite is identical to the pre-change baseline on the same commit: 224 failing files, 373 failing tests, 5199 passing, before and after.
apps/web typecheck passes and verify-decision-evidence.mjs passes 333 of 333.
